abstraction_design.rationale: The helpers and components stretch well to similar cases, but list-of-cards markup is duplicated rather than abstracted, so list-level changes are per-page.

findings.issue: The Pokémon-card list (count paragraph + <ul class="card-grid">) is hand-rolled identically in four pages (home, moves, abilities, types), so any list-level change (sorting, empty state, grid tweaks) is a 4-file edit.
findings.suggestion: Extract a PokemonCardList component (props: cards, count label, empty text) and render it from all four pages.

findings.issue: The alternate-form filter (id < MAX_SPECIES_ID) and the species-name fallback (`species.get(id) ?? (ref as unknown as Named).name`) are re-implied in getPokemonIndex too (api.ts:144), so changing form-exclusion or the fallback means editing two functions.
findings.suggestion: Extract a shared isDefaultForm(id)/resolveSpeciesName helper used by both pokemonRefsToSpecies and getPokemonIndex.

findings.issue: The fetch → DOMParser → replace-innerHTML partial-refresh script is duplicated in MoveTables.astro:119-131 (with replaceWith instead), so abort/error/refresh behaviour changes must be made twice.
findings.suggestion: Hoist a small shared client util (e.g. src/scripts/swap-region.ts) keyed on a data attribute, and call it from both scripts.

findings.issue: The type list inlines the badge class and --badge-bg custom-property hook, duplicating TypeBadge's markup/style contract.
findings.suggestion: Render TypeBadge (with link) for each type, or give the anchor the shared type-badge class.

findings.issue: Fallback `(ref as unknown as Named).name` would silently produce a Pokémon name (e.g. deoxys-normal) instead of a species name, and the cast hides that fragility.
findings.suggestion: If the species map misses, log or fall back to humanized name explicitly rather than casting the raw ref.

findings.issue: getPokemonIndex always builds species+types+generations indexes together; a page needing only part of it still pays for all three.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable for the single home-page consumer, but split per-index helpers if more pages need them.

summary: A small, idiomatic Astro 7 SSR app whose editability rests on a single well-factored data module (api.ts) and narrow prop-driven components, so most fixes and data-source changes are one-file. Removal of a feature is exemplary — a route directory plus one self-contained section. The main tax is copy-pasted card-list markup across four pages and a duplicated client refresh script, which turn list-level and partial-refresh changes into multi-file edits.
